topics.display_title: Economic Impact of British Rule (Drain, deindustrialisation, land-revenue, famines)

panels.title: Extraction became structural underdevelopment
ascii_lines: COMPANY PLUNDER -> early direct extraction after conquest and Diwani
SYSTEMIC DRAIN -> home charges, remittances, profits, pensions and imperial costs
STRUCTURAL CHANGE -> revenue pressure, deindustrialisation and dependent trade
OUTCOME -> poverty and modernisation without autonomous development.
MUST REMEMBER: Drain, deindustrialisation, land-revenue pressure and famine vulnerability are
related mechanisms, not interchangeable slogans; Dadabhai Naoroji and R.C. Dutt made
specific economic arguments.
source_references: 21. Comparative synthesis: extraction, transformation and colonial modernisation

panels.title: Three land-revenue systems compared
ascii_lines: PERMANENT -> zamindari estate | fixed in perpetuity | Bengal-Bihar-Orissa
RYOTWARI -> individual ryot | periodic revision | Madras-Bombay
MAHALWARI -> village or mahal | periodic revision | north-west and Punjab
COMMON CORE -> cash demand and secure colonial revenue, with different risk carriers.
source_references: 3. The Permanent Settlement, 1793: Cornwallis, zamindar property and fixed demand
4. The Ryotwari settlement: Read, Munro, and direct settlement with uncertainty
5. The Mahalwari settlement: Holt Mackenzie's framework and Bird's implementation
6. Comparative synthesis of the three land-revenue systems

panels.title: Commercialisation shifted risk downward
ascii_lines: EXPORT DEMAND / PLANTER ADVANCE -> cash-crop commitment
REVENUE CALENDAR + CREDIT -> dependence on moneylender or planter
PRICE / HARVEST SHOCK -> cultivator bears the loss while claims remain due
RESULT -> indebtedness, land alienation and differentiated agrarian protest.
source_references: 7. Commercialisation: crops, coercion, credit and risk
19. Poverty, demography, indebtedness and ecological/social variation

panels.title: Indigo, Pabna and Deccan were not one movement
ascii_lines: INDIGO 1859-60 -> European planters -> collective refusal to sow
PABNA FROM 1873 -> zamindars -> leagues, rent resistance and litigation
DECCAN 1875 -> moneylenders -> seizure and destruction of debt bonds
EXAM RULE -> match target, grievance and repertoire before comparing outcomes.
source_references: 8. Case studies in economic protest: Indigo, Pabna, Deccan

panels.title: Deindustrialisation was a causal web
ascii_lines: ENGLISH MECHANISATION -> cheaper factory cloth
TARIFF ASYMMETRY -> unequal access to British and Indian markets
COURT DECLINE -> lost elite demand for fine crafts
RAIL PENETRATION -> imports reach interior markets
RESULT -> uneven output and employment decline, not total craft extinction.
source_references: 11. Artisan displacement, de-urbanisation and the limits of "deindustrialisation"

panels.title: The 2024 how-far answer
ascii_lines: NECESSARY CONDITION -> Industrial Revolution lowered British production costs
TRANSMISSION MECHANISMS -> tariffs, political power, court decline and rail access
VARIATION -> region, craft and timing prevent a total-extinction claim
VERDICT -> substantially responsible, but not sufficient without colonial policy.
source_references: 10. The 2024 "how far" demand: Industrial Revolution and Indian handicrafts

panels.title: Drain theory names channels, not an invented total
ascii_lines: INDIAN REVENUE -> home charges and India Office costs
OFFICIAL INCOME -> salaries, pensions and private remittances
BRITISH CAPITAL -> profits, interest and guaranteed returns
IMPERIAL PROCUREMENT / WAR -> stores and external costs charged to India
RULE -> explain mechanism and significance; do not invent a percentage.
source_references: 12. Drain theory: plunder, systemic drain and its channels
13. Naoroji, R.C. Dutt and M.G. Ranade: the nationalist economic critique

panels.title: Export surplus could finance transfer
ascii_lines: INDIAN EXPORTS EXCEED VISIBLE IMPORTS -> apparent trade surplus
COUNCIL-BILL MECHANISM -> sterling claims and rupee payments connect the accounts
HOME CHARGES / REMITTANCES -> surplus services external obligations
ANALYTICAL POINT -> a surplus need not mean resources remained available in India.
source_references: 14. Export surplus, Council Bills and the colonial fiscal-financial system

panels.title: Infrastructure had a dual effect
ascii_lines: IMPERIAL DESIGN -> troops, administration, raw-material export and import reach
FINANCING -> private British capital protected through the Guarantee System
UNINTENDED EFFECT -> market integration and later nationalist mobility
SAFE VERDICT -> modern infrastructure without autonomous developmental priority.
source_references: 15. Infrastructure: railways, ports, roads, telegraph, canals and forests

panels.title: Colonial industrialisation was real but constrained
ascii_lines: GROWTH -> plantations, jute, cotton, coal, mines and later steel
OWNERSHIP -> foreign capital remained powerful in key sectors
CONSTRAINTS -> finance, policy bias, technology and narrow domestic demand
VERDICT -> industry developed unevenly; deindustrialisation did not mean zero industry.
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Permanent, Ryotwari and Mahalwari settlements differed by region,
assessment unit and intermediary structure; no one settlement covered all India or remained
unchanged in practice.
source_references: 16. Colonial industrialisation: plantations, mines and modern industry

panels.title: Famine was shock plus structural amplification
ascii_lines: CLIMATE / HARVEST SHOCK -> immediate scarcity risk
REVENUE RIGIDITY + COMMERCIALISATION -> weak household buffers
PRICE-LED TRANSPORT + LAISSEZ-FAIRE RELIEF -> entitlement failure
ADMINISTRATIVE DELAY -> mortality and distress deepen
RULE -> avoid both climate-only and export-only explanations.
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Nationalist, Marxist and revisionist scholarship must be tied to wage, trade,
craft, revenue and mortality evidence, with regional variation and data limits made
explicit.
source_references: 17. Famine causation: climate shock versus entitlement and governance
18. The famine case sequence and colonial famine policy

panels.title: Historiography and final synthesis
ascii_lines: NATIONALIST -> drain and deindustrialisation explain poverty
STRUCTURAL -> dependent integration into world capitalism
REVISIONIST -> disputes scale and measurement, not all structural change
REGIONAL -> outcomes varied by place, sector and social group
SYNTHESIS -> extraction and transformation must be assessed together.
source_references: 21. Comparative synthesis: extraction, transformation and colonial modernisation
